source: US Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department API
notes: Raw responses preserved without numerical modification. No expected values were generated by PrayerTime.
USNO uses UT1; the app represents UTC. Their difference is below one second, relevant only to subsecond comparisons.
Rise/set definition: geometric solar center altitude -0.8333 degrees, sea-level level unobstructed horizon, average atmospheric assumptions. The alpha model uses -0.833 degrees.

Rise/set/transit service outputs minute precision. A 60-second moderate-latitude development comparison tolerance covers reference quantization and the alpha model approximation; it is not an observational accuracy claim.
The tz argument here already includes the actual desired UTC offset; dst=false avoids the API applying US daylight-saving rules to other countries.
Solar-coordinate celnav responses include all objects. Select properties.data entry object=Sun and its almanac_data dec/gha/hc fields for comparisons; these are degrees.
At 12:00 UT1, signed Sun GHA divided by 15 gives equation-of-time hours. Compare with an explicit approximate-model tolerance.
City names are labels. Test inputs are the exact embedded coordinates.

sundata.phen: Object continuously above the Twilight Limit
